entries.claim: FORMAT.md says a tag on a `## ` heading line fails the check because the check reads headings exactly, but the spine and epic heading regex `^(S|E-\d{2,}): \S` (lib/check.mjs:94) only anchors the ID prefix, so `[ASSUMPTION]` after the heading text passes.
entries.failure_scenario: Copy samples/, change spine.md to `## S-01: Loans are an append-only event log [ASSUMPTION]` and epics.md to `## E-01: Catalog [ASSUMPTION]`, then run `node lib/check.mjs <dir>`. It prints `seldon check: all four documents conform` and exits 0 (reproduced). A drafter that counts on the check to catch tags in forbidden places, as the doc promises, ships tagged spine and epic headings. Those headings carry into Cadence as decision and epic names.

entries.claim: The sample brief, which FORMAT.md:3 says conforms, breaks the new own-words contract. Most of its items have neither a `> ` quote nor an `[ASSUMPTION]` tag, and FORMAT.md:152/162/169 says untagged text is the user's own and must carry its source phrase quoted below it, while an item with no source words must carry `[ASSUMPTION]`.
entries.failure_scenario: samples/brief.md has untagged, unquoted items under Solution (line 9), Who it serves (12), What's different (15), Success criteria (18-19), Scope (22), What it refuses (25, 28) and Vision (31). Only Problem and the reservations refusal carry a quote. Under FORMAT.md each of these is either the user's words without the required quote or a guess without the required tag, so the reference sample models output the contract forbids. FORMAT.md's own Examples brief has the same gap: its refusal bullet (line 236) and Success criteria (line 230) are untagged and unquoted. The check passes all of it because it doesn't read quotes or tags.

entries.claim: A section or free-text field whose whole body is just `[ASSUMPTION]` passes the non-empty test. That contradicts FORMAT.md:154 ('text there checks the same with or without it') and FORMAT.md:149 (the tag goes right after the guessed text it marks).
entries.failure_scenario: In a brief-only folder, replace the Vision body with the single line `[ASSUMPTION]` and run `node lib/check.mjs --brief <dir>`. It prints `seldon check: brief.md conforms` and exits 0 (reproduced). Remove the tag and the same section fails with `brief.md: Vision: empty section`, so the tag alone turns a fail into a pass. The same goes for an epic field such as `**Outcome:** [ASSUMPTION]` (check.mjs:147-148). A fast-path draft with no guess for a section can pass with no content at all.
